business_problem: Decentralized business-unit data practices and complex analytics tooling made it hard for nontechnical users to discover the right data, understand schemas, and get answers quickly.
solution_summary: TUI standardized enterprise analytics on Snowflake so governed travel, customer, and operational data could support both classic reporting and new AI-driven discovery workflows. The Technology Analytics team runs Snowflake on AWS as the backbone for data across airlines, hotels, agencies, cruises, and internal business functions. On top of that foundation, TUI built TACO, an AI assistant powered by Cortex Analyst that uses semantic models to let users ask natural-language questions against approved schemas. In parallel, Cortex Search indexes enterprise metadata so employees can locate data products, understand who owns them, and discover where key data sits without manually digging through separate tools. The same indexing work also surfaced data-quality issues that TUI fixed as part of rollout. By keeping core data, semantic modeling, metadata search, and user-facing AI on one governed platform, TUI improved self-service access while reducing demand on central data teams.

solution_components.name: Cortex Analyst

solution_components.name: Cortex Search

data_flow: Business-unit data is centralized in Snowflake on AWS. Cortex Analyst uses semantic models on top of governed schemas to answer natural-language questions, while Cortex Search indexes metadata so employees can find datasets, owners, and data products through TUI's discovery interfaces.
business_outcome: TUI built AI data-discovery prototypes in hours, answered more than 500 complex natural-language queries during early testing, and expects each use case to save more than 30 days of people time while improving data quality and responsiveness.
